name: Urban Meadows and Lawns: Choosing the Most Appealing Green Space (Tübingen)
description: Faithful replication with the original photographs: the authors' photographs of green spaces in Tubingen, Germany, digitally edited into scenarios that differ in the type of green space (natural meadow, unnatural green space with a non-native bright-flowered seed mixture, or lawn), in whether a regularly mowed acceptance stripe borders the meadow, and, in front of three buildings in the city, in the size of the asphalt forecourt (large, small or only a pathway). Participants see the paper's Questions 1, 2.1, 2.2 and 2.3 in turn, each a set of pictures in random order, as in the paper, and choose the scenarios they find most appealing: up to two of the eight pictures in Question 1 and up to three of the nine pictures in each of Questions 2.1-2.3, as in the paper. They then answer the paper's sociodemographic categories from its Table 1: age group, gender, whether they have children, whether they are a student, commitment to nature conservation, and self-perception as a country type or city type. Rebuilt from Zobec, Betz & Unterweger (2020), Perception of Urban Green Areas Associated with Sociodemographic Affiliation, Structural Elements, and Acceptance Stripes, Urban Science 4(1): 9, with the photographs from its Figures 1-4 and the task from Section 2.1 (CC BY 4.0). Image ids: q1_A-q1_H and q21_A-q23_I = question and scenario letter as in Figures 1-4; answers are in q1, q21, q22 and q23 as lists of the chosen image ids; each image's scenario label is stored in the page's original-study block. Analysis as in the paper: number of choices for each scenario, Pearson chi-squared cross-tables of the chosen scenarios against each sociodemographic group with standardized residuals beyond +/-2 as significant, with choices projected to the maximum number when a participant chose fewer. The paper (1367 people recruited through the University of Tubingen mailing list, 67% of whom completed the survey; mean age 31, 68% women) found that people with an affinity for city life preferred natural meadows when an acceptance stripe was mowed along their margins, and that 40- to 60-year-olds rejected intensely maintained lawns. Differences from the original study: (1) the paper's Question 3 (meadows and lawns with benches, lanterns and a sculpture) is left out, because four of its twelve pictures contain a lantern photograph from FreeImages.com that is not under the paper's CC BY licence; (2) the question wording, the instruction text and the set titles are ours, because the paper only says participants chose the scenarios they found most appealing; the picture numbers shown on screen are ours; (3) the paper's faculty question, specific to the University of Tubingen, is left out, and the wording of the other background questions is ours with the paper's categories; (4) the paper ran on Unipark through the university mailing list in 2016; here anyone can take part; (5) the photographs are the figure copies (about 430-700 px wide).
